source_text: Et re vera multo ego consequentius unum, quem Apostolus dicit, unum assero, ut doceam vitium imitationis, non generationis fuisse, quam Traducianus unius nomine, qui dicitur peccati fuisse vestibulum, seminibus rem admovet voluntatis, quod rerum natura non recipit.
pass_a_gloss: And in truth I much more consequently assert that the one whom the Apostle says is one, so that I may teach that the vice was of imitation, not of generation, than the Traducianus, by the name of one who is said to have been the vestibule of sin, moves a matter of will to seeds, which the nature of things does not receive.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS semen; Blaise bodily seed vs transmitted sin
Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: Indeed, I am far more consistent in maintaining that the one whom the apostle names is one, to show that the fault lay in imitation, not generation. The advocate of inherited sin, by contrast, uses the name of the one said to be sin’s gateway to attach a matter of will to seed—something the nature of things does not permit (compare Romans 5:12) (Romans 5:12).

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
